newsitem.title: BRUNEI: Brunei signs US$1 bln refinery agreement.
newsitem.headline: Brunei signs US$1 bln refinery agreement.

text.p: Brunei on Wednesday signed a memorandum of understanding with Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) and Japan's Kanematsu Corp to build a US$1 billion refinery and petrochemical complex.
The pact represented the oil-rich country's first step towards developing its petrochemical industry, Brunei's Deputy Minister of Finance Selamat Munap told reporters after inking the pact.
"This is a first step..It will help to vitalise Brunei's economy further," he said. "This is a natural progression in Brunei's oil industry which hitherto had been a net crude oil exporter."
Under the agreement, the new complex will include a 60,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery
The complex would also include an aromatics plant to produce and export 420,000 tonnes of paraxylene a year and 200,000 tonnes of benzene a year.
Masami Kido, Kanematsu managing director, said the products of the plant are the basic feedstock for various petrochemical industries.
The planned project represents another move by the sultanate to expand its energy sector away from reliance on crude production.
Brunei produces 165,000 bpd of crude oil, most of which is exported. It has a small 9,000 bpd refinery serving its population of 270,000.
In May, Brunei signed a letter of intent to build a 160,000 bpd refinery at a cost of $1.5 billion with state-owned German engineering group IAB.
